RFC 8017 defines RSA-PSS as a signature encoding plus RSA private-key signature primitive, not generic private-key encryption of a hash; author wording distinguishes the textbook shorthand.
RFC 8032 specifies EdDSA/Ed25519 and deterministic signing behavior; the lesson limits the claim to deterministic nonce derivation and does not imply all implementation risks disappear.

NIST announced FIPS 203 ML-KEM, FIPS 204 ML-DSA and FIPS 205 SLH-DSA on 2024-08-13; used to verify names and algorithm roles.
Official ML-KEM standard; describes KEM role, parameter sets and Module-LWE relation. NIST planning note identifies a potential update, so pedagogical text avoids claims of absolute proof.
Official ML-DSA digital-signature standard.
Official SLH-DSA stateless hash-based signature standard derived from SPHINCS+.
IETF RFC 4033 confirms DNSSEC data-origin authentication and integrity, and explicitly excludes confidentiality and DoS protection; used to qualify the lesson scope.

IETF RFC 8484 defines DNS over HTTPS and notes TLS confidentiality/integrity for the HTTPS exchange; lesson distinguishes transport protection from DNSSEC record validation and notes traffic analysis metadata.
IETF RFC 7858 specifies default DoT over TCP port 853; used to check the source’s port statement.
BCP 38 ingress filtering is a best-practice recommendation to reduce packets with forged source addresses; the lesson presents it as mitigation, not universal deployment.
Official Nmap guide confirms SYN/connect scan mechanics and state interpretation. The lesson qualifies “stealth” as relative: detection/logging can still occur.

WireGuard protocol specification confirms Noise_IKpsk2_25519_ChaChaPoly_BLAKE2s construction and the protocol’s fixed primitive suite; lesson avoids treating formal/model analysis or smaller code as proof of absolute superiority.

Original KRACK researchers describe replayed handshake messages causing key reinstallation and reset of nonce/replay counters. Lesson frames impact as implementation-dependent and does not say WPA2’s cipher was broken.

Systematization paper supports the distinction that transient/speculative execution can leave secret-dependent microarchitectural traces; the lesson distinguishes Meltdown from Spectre and avoids treating one mitigation as universal.

Linux kernel documentation confirms seccomp filter decisions use syscall metadata/arguments, BPF filter actions are configurable, and installation has privilege/no_new_privs conditions; lesson avoids claiming every denied syscall must kill the process.
TCG guidance distinguishes Secure Boot (verify next-stage signature before execution) from Measured Boot (record measurements); measured boot alone does not prevent execution.

Debian tracker describes malicious code in upstream xz tarballs extracted by the liblzma build process; the text distinguishes this release/build compromise from Thompson’s compiler self-propagation thought experiment.

Linux kernel documentation says Rust was merged in v6.1 to assess suitability and describes support as under development/experimental for some configurations; lesson does not imply general production readiness.
